conclusion: Verified: The cited MISEV2023 guidance (ev-misev2023-quality-framework) supports the high-level requirement that transparent, orthogonal characterization, separation from non-vesicular particles, appropriate controls, and fit-for-purpose, validated intact‑EV assays are needed to de-risk identity and potency claims and to justify cross‑species in vivo/bridging studies. Not verified / Unsupported by the supplied evidence: any program‑specific assertions that SGL‑001 already meets those CMC/analytics gating criteria (MCB/WCB generation and characterization, validated orthogonal intact‑EV assays with LLOQ/specificity/precision, stability‑indicating potency assays, and reproducible release/stability/potency across ≥3 GMP‑like batches), and any claim that rodent intranasal biodistribution data alone predict intact‑EV CNS exposure in larger species for SGL‑001. The single supplied evidence item provides consensus guidance but contains no program data to demonstrate implementation or to justify advancing formulation/bridging studies without the program deliverables described in the proposed next actions.
unsupported_assertions: SGL-001 source‑cell materials and manufacturing (MCB/WCB) are characterized and scalable (no MCB/WCB records or scale‑up/validation data in supplied evidence).
Validated orthogonal intact‑EV QC/assays for SGL‑001 are in place (no assay validation reports with LLOQ, specificity, precision provided).
Stability‑indicating, mechanism‑linked potency assay correlated to an in vivo PD endpoint is established for SGL‑001 (no potency/stability assay data provided).
Reproducible release, stability, and potency comparability across ≥3 representative GMP‑like batches has been demonstrated for SGL‑001 (no batch records, release, or comparability data provided).

Rodent intranasal biodistribution data for SGL‑001 alone are sufficient to predict intact‑EV CNS exposure in larger species (MISEV2023 recommends orthogonal analytics and bridging; it does not provide program data showing translatability).
